mainLinks.per: percentage point of GDP the federal deficit changes, in basis points
mainLinks.anchor: A one point rise in the projected federal deficit over GDP raises long-term interest rates about 25 basis points, and the rates states pay to borrow move with them. A law that cuts spending lowers what every state pays; a law that spends more raises it. Markets price the projected deficit when the law is made, so there is no lag. The paper's summary gives no band, so the spread is the default for researched links, 25% either way.
mainLinks.source: Laubach 2009, New Evidence on the Interest Rate Effects of Budget Deficits and Debt, Journal of the European Economic Association 7(4): 858-885; the deficit change from data/research/federal/federal-outlay-terms-fy2025.json (Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement, BEA, CBO)

mainLinks.per: percent of what the state produces that extra defense contracts add
mainLinks.group: workers in the states that get the contracts
mainLinks.anchor: A state that gets a dollar more of military procurement than others gets about $1.50 more output. Earnings are read to move one for one with output, so each percent of the state's output that extra contracts add lifts earnings 1.5%. The extra contracts follow a build-up at the pace defense contracts rose in the years they beat inflation, in each state in proportion to the contracts it drew in 2024 (data/research/federal/defense-contracts-by-state-fy2024.json). The paper's summary gives no band, so the spread is the default for researched links, 25% either way. The effect is read the same year the money is spent, since the study measures it within the year and the build-up already phases in over the years of the law.
mainLinks.source: Nakamura and Steinsson 2014, Fiscal Stimulus in a Monetary Union: Evidence from U.S. Regions, American Economic Review 104(3), NBER w17391; contracts from USAspending.gov and output from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, read September 29, 2026

mainLinks.per: percent more intercity rail riders a federal expansion plan projects
mainLinks.anchor: A federal law that pays to expand passenger rail funds the plan Amtrak asked Congress for: 62.5% more riders over 15 years, with the first added service 30 months in (src/simulation/federal-passenger-rail.ts). Rail ridership forecasts come true only in part: across 25 rail projects, actual traffic averaged 51.4% below forecast, with a standard deviation of 28.1 points. The timing is the plan's own, so the link acts in the month the plan's riders arrive. Provisional: the projection is Amtrak's, not a measured result of a past federal law.

mainLinks.per: percent of the state's farm real estate value that the payments cut removes each year
mainLinks.anchor: Each $1 of government payments per acre is worth $13 to $30 per acre of farmland value; the middle is $21.50. A payments cut equal to 1% of a state's farm real estate value each year lowers its land values by 21.5%, and the spread is the paper's own.
